items.stem: Briefly explain why diseconomies of scale may occur as a business grows.
items.answer: Longer chains of command slow communication and decision-making, coordination becomes harder, and employees may feel alienated and less motivated, so average costs rise.

items.stem: NordBike Ltd has fixed costs of $40,000 a month and variable costs of $15 per unit. If it expands output from 5,000 to 10,000 units, bulk buying will reduce variable cost per unit by 10%. Calculate the average cost per unit before and after expansion, and identify two types of economy of scale involved.
items.answer: Before: $23; after: (40,000 + 13.50 × 10,000)/10,000 = $17.50. Economies: spreading fixed costs over more units (technical/indivisibilities) and purchasing (bulk-buying) economies.
items.markingKey: AC1 = 23.00; new VC = 13.50; AC2 = 17.50. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both average costs. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Economies of scale are the main reason why businesses grow."
items.answer: Economies of scale are a major motive, but firms also grow for market power, security and ambition, and growth only lowers costs up to a point.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: lower average costs; pricing power and competitiveness; financial and marketing advantages. Arguments against: market power and reduced competition; diversification of risk; managerial ambition; diseconomies may outweigh savings. Supported judgement: Economies of scale are a major motive, but firms also grow for market power, security and ambition, and growth only lowers costs up to a point.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "economies of scale".

items.stem: "A business with high revenue is always large in every other way." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Measures of size can disagree: a trading firm may have high revenue but few employees and little capital employed.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "strategic alliance".
items.answer: An agreement between businesses to cooperate on a project while remaining independent and without forming a new company

items.stem: Which of the following is an internal economy of scale?
options: A pool of skilled workers in the region
Local training colleges for the industry
A large firm obtaining cheaper loans from banks
items.answer: A large firm obtaining cheaper loans from banks
items.markingKey: C. Financial economies are internal.

items.stem: Which is the most common way of measuring business size in many countries?
items.answer: Number of employees
items.markingKey: Number of employees. The EU defines SMEs by headcount and turnover.

items.stem: Yusuf writes: "MNCs always exploit host countries." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Impacts vary: MNCs can create jobs, pay above local wages and transfer skills, though some exploit weak regulation; outcomes depend on host-country policies.
items.markingKey: Impacts vary: MNCs can create jobs, pay above local wages and transfer skills, though some exploit weak regulation; outcomes depend on host-country policies. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between a takeover and a merger.
items.answer: A merger is an agreed combination of two firms into one; a takeover (acquisition) is the purchase of a controlling stake in one firm by another, sometimes against its management's wishes.
items.markingKey: A merger is an agreed combination of two firms into one; a takeover (acquisition) is the purchase of a controlling stake in one firm by another, sometimes against its management's wishes. items.answer: Small size brings flexibility, personal service and control; large size brings economies of scale, market power, easier finance and the ability to diversify risk.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the host country and the home country.
items.answer: The home country is where the MNC is headquartered; the host country is where it operates subsidiaries or production but is not headquartered.
